Phrasal Verbs
Phrasal verbs are two-word verbs made out of a verb and a preposition or adverb.
Today, we go on with our last lesson about manuals.
Let's go over the basic considerations you may have to keep in mind when creating an effective manual.

There are some phrasal verbs that are separable, this means that you can separate the verb from the preposition or adverb when the action affects directly an object or object pronoun (me, you, him, her, it, uLet's go over the basic considerations to keep in mind when creating an effective manual.s, them.)

Example: 

Turn off


The system is programmed to turn off the updates.
The system is programmed to turn the updated off.

The system is programmed to turn it off. (Correct)
The system is programmed to turn off it. (Incorrect)

Some other phrasal verbs inseparable, so these words need to remain together, they cannot be separated.

Example: 

Work on


We are working on a new architecture style.

Tips to Write an Effective User Manual
These are some important tips to consider when you write a manual.
You should also have clear the purpose of your manual and let the reader know it.
Select the appropriate information and make it easy to understand.

Before you write a manual you should consider some important tips to help you develop your ideas better.

Pay close attention to the following tips:

  1. Don’t assume: Not all users know the same things you do, don’t take for granted important pieces of information.
  1. Plan your purpose: You need to have clear ideas of what you want to explain, otherwise, you’ll end up writing about lots of things.
  1. Outline it: Before you get to write the content itself, plan what you want to write, create a draft of how your manual will look like.
  1. Keep it short: Don’t overwhelm users with tons of information, be specific and try to go straight to the point.
  1. Keep it simple: Select words carefully, you might need to create a glossary if you too many technical terms.
  1. Use visual aids: If you need to illustrate an idea, introduce pictures or diagrams to make sure the readers get your idea.

User Manuals

Today, we go on with our last lesson about manuals. Let’s go over the basic considerations you may have to keep in mind when creating an effective manual. First, you might need to get out of your own mind. By this, I mean you should think of the person who is going to read the manual. Do not take anything for granted unless you know you’re writing for a specialized audience.

You should also have clear the purpose of your manual and let the reader know it. This way you’ll avoid wasting users’ time. It’s important you plan what you’re going to write before you just jump to do it. Select the appropriate information and make it easy to understand; not all users comprehend all the technical terms, try to use synonyms and add a glossary if necessary. If you feel you need to explain difficult instructions, do not hesitate and insert images and diagrams, they help you illustrate concepts. Before you decide if it is the final version of your manual, ask someone to read it and be open to feedback. Sometimes we think we’re clear, but we might not use the right words or grammatical structures.

Let’s move on to the next point, how to write an outline for a user manual. First, you need to choose carefully the parts you consider must be in the manual. Write an introductory page, describing the main components and functions. Write the body of the manual, and remember to read after you’re done. This helps you avoid typos and confusing ideas. If you need a graphic, draw a sketch, write the main ideas and move on. Finally, you’ll need to add the table of contents and contact information for further questions.

Making an Outline of a User Manual

Create a short outline of a user manual for a product of your choice. (150-170 words)

  • Think about the product and what it is used for.
  • Make a list of the steps necessary to use the product well.
  • Think about the visual aids you could need to explain the product and its uses.

Instructions:

  • Create the outline of the user manual (150-170 words)
  • Use first a paragraph to describe the product and what its uses are.
  • Write all the necessary instructions to use the product.
  • Describe the visual aids you may need.
